div.div: بَخْتَرِىٌّ and ↓ بِخْتِيرٌ Elegant, or beautiful, in gait and in body; (L, K: in [some of] the copies of the K, instead of وَالجِسْمِ, is erroneously put وَالجَسِيمُ: TA:) applied to a man: (L:) or (so accord. to the L and TA, but in the K “ and ”) proud and self-conceited: (L, K:) or who walks in the manner termed تَبَخْتُرٌ [see Q. 2.]: (JK, L:) the former epithet is also applied to a camel: (L:) the fem. of the former is with ة. (JK, L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
